conviction_note: The Q3 margin was already given out at the 5 Oct pre-close call (adj. EBIT margin 'rather on the 3% side'), so the move sits in the FY guide. Hitting even the low end of 3.0-4.0% needs a Q4 margin of about 5.2-5.4% after a 9M margin near 2.2%, and both 2026 prints were sold intraday. Against that, Q3 cash was flagged as solid and the stock is already -9.5% over 20 days. That gives a mild negative lean (p_up 45) on a 6% absolute move, -0.6 scaled, against an impact_sum of -0.7. The two numbers agree in sign and size.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide (adj. EBIT margin 3.0-4.0% on EUR17.0-17.5bn) needs a Q4 margin of about 5.2-5.4% just to reach the low end. H1 was EUR157m (1.8%) and Q3 is steered to ~3% on trough sales, so 9M is near 2.2%. On the call management would not commit within the range: 'there are also some risks ... we have to discuss that when we are getting closer to the end of year'. Jefferies asked whether recoveries could slip into 2027 because peers were flagging it. Expect a narrowing to the low end, with a cut as the tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 30 Jul 2026 ad-hoc guide cut paired with the BMW settlement and >EUR1bn awards: the stock jumped. 6 Aug H1 with buyback framework: initially up, then fell almost 5% in the afternoon. 7 May Q1 beat with guide confirmed: -2.6% after midday. Prints with an unchanged guide have been sold.
findings.original_quote: With all the changes we have, for sure there are also some risks, but that's the normal course of the business. So we have to discuss that when we are getting closer to the end of year.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: stock3 wrote 'das Jahresziel verlangt ein starkes Q4' on 6 Oct and the stock is -9.5% over 20 days (-13% from 7 Oct). What is not priced is the outcome of the guide decision itself, which will be taken in the release. If the market expected an outright cut, the stock would trade at its Aug lows or below rather than around EUR34, and shorts would be building rather than flat at 0.6%.
findings.independence: Visteon (8-K, 22 Oct 2026) lowered its FY EBITDA guide on warranty and electronics cost pressures: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001111335/000111133526000054/visteonq32026pr.htm. Arithmetic from the 30 Jul ad-hoc and the 6 Aug H1 release.

findings.finding: The Q3 adj. EBIT margin was pre-released at about 3% (lower end of 3-4%) at the 5 Oct pre-close call. The reference sheet attributes it to timing: cost increases for raw materials and memory are booked in Q3, and the larger part of the customer recoveries in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 was pre-released by ad-hoc on 30 Jul, and the 6 Aug report moved on the capital-allocation and guide narrative rather than on the pre-released figures.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. The company told the market, and the German press repeated it on 6 Oct ('Q3-Marge nahe 3 %'). Filed at 0 per the rule on pre-released numbers.

findings.finding: The Q3 reference sheet flags Q3 cash as solid: 'cash performance benefited from continued spending discipline, controlled CapEx and solid net working capital management', despite the EUR100m first BMW payment (fully in adjusted FCF, one third in normalized). The remaining ~EUR250m falls in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to a FCF surprise on this name. Press after H1 (boerse-express 'Cashflow überzeugt') treated cash as the positive.
findings.why_not_priced: The sheet is qualitative and gives no number, so the size of the cash beat against the EUR500-700m normalized FCF guide is still unknown. The stock gained +7.7% over 6-7 Oct after the pre-close and gave all of it back on 8 Oct, so whatever was read into the call is no longer in the price. Management also warned of 'selective inventory increases', which caps the upside.

findings.finding: Closest US peer Visteon (22 Oct) cut FY adj. EBITDA to $370-410m from $455-495m on $77m of exceptional warranty charges and cost pressures. AMV0 fell 6.0% that day (35.25 to 33.15) and a further 1.8% the next. Aumovio's own release will carry its first statement on how 2027 memory costs are to be shared with customers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The read-across was already taken on 22-23 Oct (-7.8% over two sessions on the Yahoo tape).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the 22 Oct drop is visible on the tape. What is left is whether Aumovio's 2027 memory mechanism lands better or worse than Visteon's warning. Aumovio said it is 'not over-indexed in memory content' and that 2026 supply is secured, which argues the residual is small.
findings.independence: Yahoo tape https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/AMV0.DE?range=3mo&interval=1d shows the 22-23 Oct move

findings.finding: Continental (4 Nov) put global Q3 light-vehicle production at about -1.6% y/y, against the -2.3% Aumovio cited from September S&P data. Europe was flat, North America -5%, China -6%. It also said weak automotive markets weighed on original-equipment business and higher raw-material costs will hit harder in Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: Published the day before the print, so it may not be fully absorbed, but it is a macro proxy and the gap is 0.7 pt of production. Aumovio says its raw materials are largely indexed, which offsets the Q4 raw-material warning.

findings.finding: On the pre-close call, management described order intake as 'okay-ish ... a touch better than we have seen the trends earlier in the year' and cited BMW business awards of EUR1.5bn. It confirmed Aurora revenue from H2 2027, with 'no postponements'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The BMW award news on 30 Jul came with a jump in the stock, though it was bundled with the settlement.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 order-intake figure has not been published. Guidance only described it in words, and German press coverage of the call focused on the margin.
